## 2026-09-15 — the tour finished, and three sentences the product had stopped meaning

Chapters 9 to 13 of `docs/tutorial/`, which closes the series at thirteen. The subjects
were the five the index had listed as missing since the tour was written: the anomaly
worklist, the glossary and the naming lanes, the doorway panel, threads and the trail, and
the command line. Nine screenshots, all driven against the live dashboard on the map this
tutorial has used throughout — DunneFlow reading its own source at `1e76c51`, held against
a sealed snapshot of `875499c`.

**The map was deliberately not re-analysed.** One src file has moved since it was made, and
re-reading the tree would have drifted every number in chapters 1 to 8 away from the
screenshots beside them. Thirteen chapters quoting one reading is worth more than five
chapters quoting a fresher one, and the index now says which reading in as many words.

### What the chapters are for

Chapter 9 is the worklist, and it lands on the third triage button — *this is a DunneFlow
defect, not the program's*. It has something to press: **eight of the eleven ONE_WAY_TABLE
findings are not tables.** `json_each` is SQLite's own table-valued function, `m`, `top`,
`looped` and `mv` are CTEs in `web/queries.py`, and `reach` and `back` are the recursive
CTEs in `store.py` that compute reachability — so the tool is reporting a defect in the
machinery behind the cover's own *commands 393 routines*. The blind spot printed beside
each one was already a sentence away from naming the cause. The other three are correct:
`sqlite_master`, and `doc_tables`/`doc_table_rows`, which really are written and never read.

It also gets the denominator lesson for free. `459 of 863` against the cover's `925`, which
is 62 module scopes, and the chapter runs the query rather than asserting it.

Chapter 10 turned out to be the one with the most to say, because DunneFlow's own map has
all three naming lanes in three different states at once: **10 derived conventions, 0
stated rules from 26 documents, and 3 imported rules checked.** The same population reached
from two directions agrees to the row — `Classes are named in PascalCase` is 113 of 124 as
a derived convention graded D, and 113 of 124 as `naming.md:13` measured over the
population its own document declares. The eleven exceptions are the product.

Chapter 11 is the doorway panel, and the specimen chain is the point: the 731-comment card
names `web.queries`, its query returns `web.queries.<module>`, and two of the CTEs in that
same statement are two of chapter 9's phantom tables. Chapter 12 is threads and the trail,
photographed on the trail this session actually walked. Chapter 13 is the command line, and
leads with the thing that confuses everyone once: **the path is a program name, not a
directory** — `query /tmp/nowhere/dunneflow` reads the map in `./output/dunneflow`, which is
what the *"no --output given; maps go to output"* line is telling you.

### Three drifts, found by reading the product

Every one of these is a sentence on screen that had been false for days, and not one could
have been caught by a gate. That is now three sessions in a row.

**`DunneFlow cannot yet import a standard` — nine days.** Three sentences across the derived
and stated naming pages, plus the comment above `viewStated`. `22e82ff` built the import and
the comparison on 2026-09-06; the pages went on denying it while the navigator group they
sit in listed *Stated rules, checked* two rows down, and while the **foot of the stated page
itself** described what that page does. A page contradicting itself top and bottom, with a
test pinning the false half. Reworded; the test's assertion moved to the surviving true
claim, and `test_the_naming_pages_do_not_deny_a_capability_this_build_has` now refuses the
denial in any of its spellings for as long as `--standards` exists.

**Ten measures and twelve cards — eight days.** `02181ea` added two curiosity families on
2026-09-07; its own commit title says *"two curiosities"*. Four sentences in
`curiosities.py`, two in `serve.py`, one in `CLAUDE.md` and one in `BRIEFING.md` still said
ten. The panel counts its own cards at render time, so the screen said **12 measurements of
this program** directly above a module docstring that said ten — the mode toggle's defect
exactly, one pane over, and the reason the guard added here reads `len(FAMILIES)` and the
docstring together rather than interpolating a numeral into prose. The `/api/curiosities`
timing in that docstring was the ten-family measurement too, and is now the twelve-family
one `PERFORMANCE.md` already held (140 ms, was 106 ms at ten).

**`an ordinary thing for a routine to be`, under an ARTEFACT badge.** The empty-threads
sentence names a kind the pane does not know it has. Every other empty sentence beside it —
*It calls nothing this map can see*, *Everything it does, it does in memory* — is true of
whatever is selected; the subject's kind is not in hand there, so the fix was to stop naming
one.

### Verified

1,451 passed, 1 skipped (1,449 at `2dfe262`, plus the two guards above), mypy clean over 141
source files, ruff clean.

**And the citation count did not reproduce, again.** `RULES.md` and `CLAUDE.md` recorded
3,323 · 2,486 · 837 · 129; run against `2dfe262` itself it is **3,326 · 2,489 · 837 · 129**,
and this session's changes cite no rule number and move it by nothing. The previous entry
made a point of retaking the figure last and then added three citations to

**One thing deliberately not done.** `02-the-cover.jpg` and `06-comparison-direction.jpg`

## 2026-09-15 — `13-settings.md` against the live page, and a reset nobody can reach

The audit the last two sessions kept deferring. The chapter was billed in `docs/README.md`
as *"Every setting, what it does, and what it costs"*, and the honest position was that the
claim was unverified rather than known wrong. It was wrong, in four places, and the fourth
is a product finding rather than a documentation one.

The method was not reading `shell.js` — an earlier attempt to enumerate the controls out of
the source mechanically returned nothing, which is why this was still open. It was opening
the page and asking the DOM: six `.panel` sections, twenty-five `.setrow` rows, and the
label and description of each.

**What the page has.** APPEARANCE (2) · COLOUR (three sets, each with its contrast and its
separation) · HOW A PLATE ARRANGES WHAT IT HOLDS (by structure / by connection) · WHAT
OPENS, AND WHAT SHOWS (**23 rows**) · USAGE · ACCESSIBILITY. The chapter named six of the 23.

**What the chapter claimed and the page has not.**

* *"Everything on the graph HUD is here too, plus a few that live only here"* — spacing, the
  three spread axes, plate width, node sizing, plate order. **None of them is on this page.**
  They are HUD-only, which is right: they are things you move while watching what they do.
  Meanwhile the page's actual graph section — the plate layout choice, with its 328,531
  crossings down to 27,291 and its *"your browser has WebGPU"* line — was not in the chapter
  at all.
* **The three comparison overlays.** A whole section, under Settings. They are the **◆
  changes** switches in the code browser, the routine table and the worklist —
  `overlaySwitchHtml`, drawn only while `comparing()`. The cost table was good and is kept,
  under a heading that says where the switches are.
* **Row density and which panes are open** were listed as settings here. Both are persisted
  per program like everything else, and both are set where they apply.

**And there is no reset.** `settings.js` implements `resetSettings`, exports it on
`window.DunneFlowSettings`, and two tests defend its rule about naming what it cleared and
never naming a setting the reader was never offered. Nothing calls it: the only occurrence
in `shell.js` is a comment citing it. So the feature exists, is correct, is tested, and has
no door — which is design rule 16 turned inside out, a control that is wired to something
and never drawn. The chapter had been describing the dialog.

That one is **not fixed here.** Wiring a button is a product change and this was a
documentation pass; the chapter now states the truth — settings live in local storage under
a key per program, and clearing them means clearing site data — and the gap is recorded in
`BRIEFING.md` with the function's name, so the fix is an afternoon whenever it is wanted.

**What was verified and left alone.** Appearance, both rows. Colour: three sets, and *Red
and green* really is 5.34:1 at ΔE 5 against *Blue and orange*'s 4.86:1 at ΔE 43 — a set that
passes the first number and fails the second, which is the argument for printing both.
Usage, headed *local only · never leaves this machine*. Accessibility, all four limits, word
for word. The chapter's two screenshots are still accurate and were not retaken.

Two numbers in the chapter come from the page's own prose and are measurements of another
corpus rather than of whatever map is open — 4,734 routines in one navigator group, 335 of
1,395 rows too long for their row. The chapter now attributes them rather than implying they
are about the program in front of you.

## 2026-09-15 — the other fourteen chapters, read against the build

The audit the settings pass left open. Every remaining reference chapter checked claim by
claim against the running dashboard, the CLI's own `--help`, and the source where a
sentence is quoted from it. **Ten of the fourteen were wrong somewhere**; four were right.

Method, because it is the part worth keeping: quoted screen text against `grep` of the
string it is quoting; control sets against the DOM's `select` options and `data-*`
attributes rather than against a reading of `shell.js`; every CLI transcript re-run and
pasted. The browser is what catches control drift and the source is what catches wording
drift, and neither finds the other's.

### What was wrong

**16, the command line — seven quoted outputs, all stale.** `touches cmd_serve` reached
112 and reaches 118, and has grown a PROCESS row; `impact _emit` said 15 ways in and it is
14; the glossary said 44 of 153 and it is 44 of 155; `naming` graded routines **C** where
it is now **B**, at different counts; `check` said 24 suspect against 25; the `query`
example was one FILE boundary out. Every example also ran `… src --name dunneflow` while
quoting output from a map of `src/dunneflow`, which is why the qualnames carried a
`dunneflow.` prefix the current map does not. Re-run and re-pasted. `--db` and `--limit`
were undocumented anywhere and now have a line.

**6, Graph — the control reference described a control that is not there.** `follow` is
documented as *replaces / walk*; it is the **direction** control (`callers and callees ·
callers only · callees only`), and the replace/walk one is `following`, whose second option
is called *keeps the path*. Plate order has **six** options and the chapter named two;
Colour by has three and it named two; Detail's second level is labelled *one node per
file*, not *module*. Four controls were missing outright: `plates`, `unselected`
(dimmed/hidden), `collapse gaps`, and `reset sliders`.

**7, Table — two columns documented, four drawn.** `CONNECTIONS` (the in-and-out degree,
`3← 7→`) and `CHANGED` have been there long enough to be sortable and resizable like the
other two. `TABLE_COLS` is four and has been for a while.

**8, Document — "the same eight subjects are also written to disk".** The written map holds
**fourteen documents and an index**; the eight are the ones Document mode serves as
browsable tables, and the other seven have their own surfaces.

**14, Comparing — four bands where there are five.** `explained_only` is a band in its own
right, holding a routine whose *only* difference is the prose above it — which is exactly
the case a leading comment creates, since it sits outside the body. The chapter had it only
as a tag.

**5, The shell — two smaller ones.** The version strip has **two** no-comparison sentences
and the difference is the whole point of them: *this program has only one version* is a
limit, *nothing compared* is a switch. And the program menu's last entry is now **× Close
this map**, with *+ Analyze a directory…* above it.

**1, Installing — the stated reason maps grow was the wrong one.** Per-version growth is a
graph and a document store, about 130 MB on a 628-file program; the copies of source and
prose the chapter blamed are content-addressed, shared by every snapshot, and are 4 MB and
20 MB. The cheap thing was named as the expensive one.

**2, Getting the code — one exception and one imprecision.** *"The root is never written
down"* has exactly one deliberate exception, `standards.db`, which records the full path of
a standards directory because a quoted rule with no provenance is worth nothing. And the
recorded leaf is the **package root's**, not the analysed directory's — analyse
`~/code/proj/src` and the map says `proj`, which matters in a chapter whose punchline is
that the directory name is the only handle you get.

**9, Code** named the margin button's glyph `•`; it is `▾`. **12, Chasing rabbits** said
Clear drops the trail; it keeps the step you are standing on, deliberately.

### What was right

**3, the start page** · **10, Diagram** (checked in `b739118` and still true) · **11,
Shape** — its five lane names are verbatim what `/api/algorithms` serves · **15, When it
refuses** — every one of the fifteen quoted refusals exists in the source, word for word,
including all three standards refusals and the two Linux picker sentences.

### Two things found in the product, not the guide

**A code comment that misled this session inside five minutes.** `serve.py`'s picker header
said *"a dialog opens in front, and buying that is most of the code on both platforms"*, so

**`CLAUDE.md` was four milestones stale in its packaging section** — *"still to do:

### Not done

No screenshot was retaken. The capture pipeline clipped every full-resolution shot to the
